body.en: Taylor separated planning from execution. Under the planning in-charge work the instruction card clerk, route clerk, time and cost clerk and disciplinarian. Under the production in-charge work the speed boss, gang boss, repair boss and inspector. So a worker gets orders from eight specialists.

body.en: *Standardisation* sets standards for every activity; simplification removes needless varieties of products. Method study finds the best way to do a job; motion study removes unnecessary movements; time study fixes the standard time; fatigue study fixes rest intervals. The differential piece wage system pays a higher rate to workers who reach the standard output.

problem.en: Standard output is 10 units a day. Workers who make the standard or more get ₹50 per unit; others get ₹40 per unit. Worker A makes 11 units and worker B makes 9 units. Find their wages and the difference.

answer.en: A earns ₹550, B earns ₹360; the difference of ₹190 motivates B to reach the standard.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. Standard output is 10 units a day. Workers who make the standard or more get ₹50 per unit; others get ₹40 per unit. Worker A makes 11 units and worker B makes 9 units. Find their wages and the difference.

say.en: Let us work through this case together. Standard output is 10 units a day. Workers who make the standard or more get 50 rupees per unit; others get 40 rupees per unit. Worker A makes 11 units and worker B makes 9 units. Find their wages and the difference.
A reaches the standard: 11 times 50 rupees equals 550 rupees.
B is below the standard: 9 times 40 rupees equals 360 rupees.
Difference equals 550 rupees minus 360 rupees equals 190 rupees.
So the answer is A earns 550, rupees B earns 360 rupees; the difference of 190 rupees motivates B to reach the standard.
